answer: Like a trellis guiding vines, an agent economy can require each identity to stake a refundable bond tied to a verified work history before it can trade. Newcomers start at a jetty with limited access, earning reputation only by completing small, checkable tasks over time, while a shared lagoon of peer attestations records who vouched for whom. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real stake and slow, verifiable labor for each one, so Sybil farming becomes expensive and easy to trace when bad actors are slashed.
